A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 29-page versions of Symmetry-Aware GFlowNets, including Appendices A–L. Their readable text, equations, tables and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-graph and molecule-generation experiments in Section 6, plus ablation, computational-cost and additional experimental results in Appendices E, J and L.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical outcomes, including Figure 3, Table 1 and the experimental analyses in Appendices E, J and L.

M1.justification: Reward and flow scaling, atom- and fragment-based correction formulas, the likelihood estimator and the approximate correction scheme remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix K.

E1.justification: Both retain uniform-, clique- and cycle-reward graph experiments, atom- and fragment-based molecule generation, and the same molecular datasets for computational timing in Appendix J.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Vanilla, Transition Correction and PE (Ma et al., 2024), alongside the same Reward/Flow Scaling variants. The new Appendix I citations are used only as background.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix K retain the same architectures, training budgets, metrics and evaluation procedures, including 5,000 generated molecules and the correlation evaluation using 2,048 samples with M = 5.

E4.justification: The shortest-path-feature ablation in Appendix E.2, likelihood-estimation analysis, runtime scalability analysis in Appendix J.3 and fragment-frequency analysis in Appendix L.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices, including standard-deviation bands for likelihood estimation and mean/standard deviation over three training runs in Appendix J.2. No run-count, seed or statistical-procedure changes appear.

E6.justification: Numerical tables, plotted results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains exact atom reward-scaling diversity of 0.959 ± 0.01; runtime Tables 4–6 and appendix experimental results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, correction theorems and proofs in the main text and appendices are unchanged. The repaired citations in Appendix I do not alter its mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about correcting symmetry-induced bias, reward matching, likelihood estimation and generating diverse, high-reward graphs.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations and qualifications concerning delayed DB convergence, reward-dependent benefits, GNN expressiveness, predefined graph actions and fragment attachment points.

D1.justification: Code-access links, bliss/igraph implementation information, hardware and timing documentation, and Appendix K hyperparameters and processing instructions are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix I replaces two question-mark citation placeholders with Kong et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2025), and v3 adds their bibliography entries. This completes a limited attribution gap without changing the surrounding research positioning.

P1.justification: The citation placeholders are repaired and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose, terminology and section organization are unchanged apart from spacing.

P2.justification: The added references reflow the bibliography on pages 10–11, and the repaired citations rewrap Appendix I's opening paragraph. Figures and tables retain their content, design, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 identifies the two previously unresolved citations in Appendix I and supplies their bibliography entries, improving attribution and traceability. This is a limited quality gain: the methods, theory, empirical evidence, conclusions and limitations remain unchanged.
